title: Splitting the Uniqueness
statementMd:
Polar bears like *unique arrays* — that is, arrays without repeated elements.

You have got a unique array $*s*$ with length $*n*$ containing non-negative integers. Since you are good friends with Alice and Bob, you decide to split the array in two. Precisely, you need to construct two arrays $*a*$ and $*b*$ that are also of length $*n*$, with the following conditions for all $*i*$ $(1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*)$:

- $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$ are non-negative integers;
- $*s*_{*i*} = *a*_{*i*} + *b*_{*i*}$ .

Ideally, $*a*$ and $*b*$ should also be unique arrays. However, life in the Arctic is hard and this is not always possible. Fortunately, Alice and Bob are still happy if their arrays are *almost unique*. We define an array of length $*n*$ to be almost unique, if and only if it can be turned into a unique array by removing no more than ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2265c348fd0c0c2877464189b0017364c212a242.png) entries.

For example, the array $[1, 2, 1, 3, 2]$ is almost unique because after removing the first two entries, it becomes $[1, 3, 2]$. The array $[1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2]$ is not almost unique because we need to remove at least $3$ entries to turn it into a unique array.

So, your task is to split the given unique array $*s*$ into two almost unique arrays $*a*$ and $*b*$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains integer $*n*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5})$.

The second line contains $*n*$ distinct integers $*s*_{1}, *s*_{2}, ... *s*_{*n*}$ $(0 ≤ *s*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$.

## Output

If it is possible to make Alice and Bob happy (if you can split the given array), print "`YES`" (without quotes) in the first line. In the second line, print the array $*a*$. In the third line, print the array $*b*$. There may be more than one solution. Any of them will be accepted.

If it is impossible to split $*s*$ into almost unique arrays $*a*$ and $*b*$, print "`NO`" (without quotes) in the first line.

## Note

In the sample, we can remove the first two entries from $*a*$ and the second entry from $*b*$ to make them both unique.
statementZhMd:
北极熊喜欢*唯一数组*——也就是说，不含重复元素的数组。

现在有一个长度为 $*n*$、包含非负整数的唯一数组 $*s*$。由于你和 Alice、Bob 是好朋友，因此决定将这个数组拆分成两个数组。具体来说，你需要构造两个长度同样为 $*n*$ 的数组 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$，并满足对于所有 $*i*$ $(1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*)$：

- $*a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$ 是非负整数；
- $*s*_{*i*} = *a*_{*i*} + *b*_{*i*}$。

理想情况下，$*a*$ 和 $*b*$ 也应该是唯一数组。然而，北极的生活十分艰苦，这并不总是可能的。幸运的是，如果他们的数组是*近乎唯一*的，Alice 和 Bob 也会感到满意。如果一个长度为 $*n*$ 的数组可以通过删除不超过 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2265c348fd0c0c2877464189b0017364c212a242.png) 个元素变成唯一数组，则称该数组是近乎唯一的。

例如，数组 $[1, 2, 1, 3, 2]$ 是近乎唯一的，因为删除前两个元素后，它会变成 $[1, 3, 2]$。数组 $[1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2]$ 不是近乎唯一的，因为至少需要删除 $3$ 个元素才能将其变成唯一数组。

因此，你的任务是将给定的唯一数组 $*s*$ 拆分成两个近乎唯一的数组 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5})$。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个互不相同的整数 $*s*_{1}, *s*_{2}, ... *s*_{*n*}$ $(0 ≤ *s*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$。

## 输出格式

如果可以让 Alice 和 Bob 满意（即可以完成拆分），则第一行输出“`YES`”（不含引号）。第二行输出数组 $*a*$。第三行输出数组 $*b*$。可能存在多个解，输出其中任意一个均可。

如果无法将 $*s*$ 拆分成两个近乎唯一的数组 $*a*$ 和 $*b*$，则第一行输出“`NO`”（不含引号）。

## 说明

在样例中，我们可以删除 $*a*$ 的前两个元素以及 $*b*$ 的第二个元素，使它们都变成唯一数组。
